clue.text: Killer keeps awfully hot — do I not? — aiming for straight sets

indicators.note: a killer that keeps something holds it inside, so the other letters sit within

parts.note: the killer whale is the orca, and in crosswords ORC (a fearsome creature or ogre) also stands for a killer

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of hot are jumbled

parts.note: the question 'do I not?' contracts to don't I, run together as DONTI

explanation.surface: A murderer's angry rhetorical question becomes oddly linked to a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'straight sets' look like tennis but are sets of teeth. 'awfully' makes THO, and 'keeps' sets it with the contraction inside the killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodontic treatment such as braces is designed to straighten crooked teeth, the sets of the clue.

clue.text: See 2
21's clue to self-hate?

parts.note: read the full answer as a clue: the first three words are fodder and the last word the anagram signal, and together they produce these ten letters

explanation.surface: A hint about loathing oneself, attributed to the author at 21.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer itself works as a clue whose solution is 'to self-hate', since TALES OF THE rearranges to TO SELF-HATE and 'unexpected' signals the jumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of a short-story collection and TV series by Roald Dahl, the author at 21-across.

clue.text: Too old for reporting of event? Not a hundred!

indicators.note: Not here means without, so the letter for a hundred is dropped

parts.note: news coverage is the reporting of an event
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A question about news reports that sounds like a complaint about age limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond an age limit is past it, hence too old to qualify.

clue.text: Does lie perverted lead to rape?

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinister question about whether deceit ends in sexual assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads darkly, but rape here is the crop: the word placed before it gives 'oilseed rape', the yellow-flowered plant grown in British fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop is called oilseed rape, so the word placed before rape completes the plant's name.

clue.text: Fits of temper at time worker drinks?

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
rums are drinks

explanation.surface: Someone's outbursts are blamed on an employee boozing on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantrums are childish outbursts of anger, i.e. fits of temper.

clue.text: Diplomat accused of intrigues?

parts.note: French charge (accented) means charged, in other words accused
French d'affaires means of affairs, and affairs can be intrigues

explanation.surface: An envoy stands charged with plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the title in rough French translation: charged with affairs, which an English reader can take as 'accused of intrigues'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargé d'affaires is an embassy official who deputises for an ambassador, so a diplomat.

clue.text: Collapse of French work of art

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a composition is a work of art, musical or pictorial

explanation.surface: A remark about the fall of a French painting or piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposition is breaking down or decay, a collapse into constituent parts.

clue.text: Water feature? I'm not sure — dubious parallel between books

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

indicators.note: between means the jumbled letters sit inside the two book abbreviations

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

indicators.note: dubious, meaning doubtful or suspect, signals that parallel is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly describes a garden pond feature placed between bookshelves.
explanation.walkthrough: The water feature sounds like a fountain but is a plant that grows in ponds. 'dubious' makes RELLAPLA, and one word 'books' yields two abbreviations either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbrella plant, a sedge, grows in or beside water, so it is a feature of a water garden.

clue.text: Morris — is she from Paris?

parts.note: est is the French for is, as the words 'from Paris' suggest
elle is the French for she

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman named Morris is French.
explanation.walkthrough: Estelle Morris was a British Labour Education Secretary; 'from Paris' tells you to translate the two words into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Estelle Morris is a British politician, so her first name goes with that surname.

clue.text: Line — end of Central, start of Metropolitan — ascribed to the law

parts.note: Ongar was the eastern terminus of London Underground's Central line until 1994

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of Metropolitan is used

explanation.surface: A London Underground route description: one line's terminus, another's start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central and Metropolitan are London Underground lines; ONGAR, in Essex, was the far end of the Central line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the long arm of the law' credits the police with far-reaching power.

clue.text: Exaggerate what's no distance in Russia at a point

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
a verst is an old Russian unit of distance, about a kilometre
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about travelling no distance when at a particular spot in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to claim more than the truth, which is to exaggerate.

clue.text: Queen and prince coming after death

parts.note: R stands for Regina, the Latin for queen
Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: A royal couple succeed someone who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is short for rigor mortis, the stiffening that sets in after death; RIGOR is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigor mortis is the stiffness that sets in after someone dies, so rigor follows death.

clue.text: Old currency gamble?

definitions.meaning: the Irish pound before the euro
to bet, especially a small speculative wager

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish pound was replaced by the euro, and a speculative bet is a flutter in British slang.

clue.text: Report of weakly cure embracing odd bod and lunatic

definitions.note: a word said the same way as weakly, meaning once every seven days

indicators.note: embracing means the cure word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to heal is to cure

indicators.note: odd signals that the letters of bod are rearranged

parts.note: mad means lunatic

explanation.surface: A sickly patient's treatment news about an eccentric fellow and a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' signals that the definition is said aloud: weakly stands for weekly. 'odd' makes BDO, and 'embracing' has the cure wrap that with the madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebdomadal, from the Greek for seven, describes something happening every seven days.

clue.text: Emperor's clothes raised over half disease

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something means covering it, here wrapping around the half disease
in a down clue, raised means the word for clothes is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes

indicators.note: half means just the first half of the disease's name

parts.note: beriberi is a vitamin deficiency disease

explanation.surface: A take on the fable of the emperor's new clothes and a sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the fable of the emperor's new clothes. 'raised' gives TIUS, and 'over' has it cover the half of the sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiberius succeeded Augustus as the second Roman emperor.

clue.text: People like Lolita — it's a difficult thing to do

definitions.meaning: seductive young women, like Nabokov's nymphet

definitions.text: it's a difficult thing to do
definitions.meaning: read literally, to ... is to determine whether young cats are male or female, which is notoriously tricky

explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is a byword for a sexually precocious young girl, the kind of figure called a kitten in tabloid slang.

clue.text: Re-enter formation of earth

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A spacecraft coming back into the planet's atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrene means earthly or terrestrial, from the Latin terra for the ground.

clue.text: Subtle twist in Duncan Edwards' initiation

indicators.note: a twist in the letters means they are rearranged
initiation means the start, so only the first letter of Edwards' is used

explanation.surface: A fine turn in the early career of the Manchester United footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Duncan Edwards was a Manchester United footballer killed in the 1958 Munich air crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nuanced has fine shades of meaning, so it is subtle.

clue.text: King of footballers?

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the governing body of English footballers

explanation.surface: A question about who rules the football players.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famed for Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an Anglo-Saxon monarch who ruled Mercia.

clue.text: A word of comfort from another place

definitions.meaning: said soothingly, usually doubled, to someone upset

explanation.definitionFit: The soothing 'there, there' comforts someone, and the adverb also points to somewhere not here.

clue.text: In a way, left a lot of flowers for children's author

indicators.note: In means the letter for left goes inside the word for a way

parts.note: a road is a way

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, with its last letters dropped

parts.note: dahlias are garden flowers

explanation.surface: Someone drops off a big bunch of blooms along the road for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote much-loved children's books such as Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

clue.text: Devil opening the show

indicators.note: opening means only the first part of the word for a show is kept

parts.note: a demonstration is a show

explanation.surface: A fiend appears at the start of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, a devil.

clue.text: Parthian shot in sketch?

definitions.meaning: a parting remark; Parthian horsemen fired arrows while retreating, so a line delivered on the way out

explanation.definitionFit: A rough outline is a sketch, and an exit remark is jokingly a line spoken as you go out.

clue.text: Premier destroyer of romance

indicators.note: a destroyer of something breaks it up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prime minister portrayed as the killer of love.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was the British prime minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron served as British prime minister, also called premier.

clue.text: Holds forth about the purpose of posterity

indicators.note: about means the words for holds forth go around the purpose word

parts.note: to descant is to talk at length, to hold forth
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: Someone lectures on what future generations are for.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterity means all future generations, those who come after us.
